_note: The DSX Scene 2D corpus (dsx-game.md G6 — the 2D engine): `<sprite>` and the mode="2d" conventions AS DATA. THE QUAD LAW: a `<sprite src size position rotation scale color anchor flip>` lays out a TEXTURED QUAD in the node's LOCAL XY plane facing +Z, riding the node's world transform exactly like `<plane>` — in mode="2d" that IS camera-facing (the orthographic camera looks down −Z); BILLBOARDING IN 3D IS A NAMED ABSENCE, so an authored `rotation` stays meaningful. `size="w h"` is scene units; UNAUTHORED, height = 1 (defaultHeight) and width = the TEXTURE ASPECT (image width/height) at that height, falling back to 1 when the texture is unknown or not yet loaded. `anchor` names WHICH POINT OF THE QUAD `position` names (center default · top · bottom · left · right · top-left · top-right · bottom-left · bottom-right): the quad CENTER sits at offset (−ax·w, −ay·h, 0) from the node origin with ax ∈ {−½ left, 0 center, +½ right} and ay ∈ {+½ top, 0 center, −½ bottom}; an unknown word falls back to center with one diagnostic. `flip` mirrors UVs — "" (default) · any arrangement of the letters x and y ("x", "y", "xy", "yx"); any other word is no flip + one diagnostic. The texel MODULATES `color` exactly like the P4 texture law, and a texel with alpha < 0.5 is CUT OUT (the sprite silhouette — the text3d cutout path verbatim). THE SHEET LAW: `frames` is the sheet GRID — ONE number N = a SINGLE ROW (cols = N, rows = 1), TWO numbers = "cols rows" EXPLICITLY. The kernel NEVER guesses a grid: cols = ceil(√N) is WRONG and is not the law. Unauthored = 1×1 (the whole texture); a non-integer, a value < 1, or any other count of numbers falls back to 1×1 with one diagnostic. The UV RECTANGLE of frame n (ROW-MAJOR: left→right then top→bottom) is col = n mod cols, row = floor(n / cols), u0 = col/cols, u1 = (col+1)/cols, v0 = row/rows, v1 = (row+1)/rows — v0 is the frame's TOP edge (texel row 0 = the image's top, the P4 UV law verbatim); flip="x" swaps u0/u1, flip="y" swaps v0/v1. `frame` is the 0-based index to show, hole-bound like every prop (a store write animates it): the resolved value FLOORS, then CLAMPS to [0, cols·rows − 1] with one diagnostic when it was out of range (Article 7); a malformed value falls back to 0 with one diagnostic. THE FPS LAW: `fps` > 0 AUTO-ADVANCES on the SAME frame clock the P4 on:frame budget rides — never a second loop — as advanced = floor(elapsedSeconds × fps), with loop="true" (the default) wrapping index = advanced mod total and loop="false" clamping index = min(advanced, total − 1); a non-positive elapsed reads frame 0. When `fps` is authored and positive it OWNS the index and `frame` is not read; fps ≤ 0, unauthored or malformed means no auto-advance (malformed diagnosing once). THE 2D CONVENTIONS LAW: in mode="2d" the camera is ORTHOGRAPHIC with `size` the VERTICAL half-extent (half-width = size·aspect — the P1 law unchanged), +Y is UP, z is the DRAW ORDER (higher z draws IN FRONT: the renderers paint in `sceneDrawOrder2d` order — world z ASCENDING, stable in document order — with depth testing OFF, the painter's algorithm), and `position` accepts a PAIR "x y" meaning z = 0 (every OTHER vector word — rotation, scale, velocity — stays a triple, a NAMED ABSENCE; in mode="3d" a 2-number position is malformed exactly as before). There is NO pixel-space mode: units stay scene units. THE Z-LOCK PHYSICS LAW: `physics=` on a `<sprite>` runs through the EXISTING 3D solver — there is no second solver. A mode="2d" world carries a Z-LOCK: every body records zLock = its initial world z and vzLock = its initial z velocity at world creation, and the LAST act of every step (after the sleep pass, before the tick advances) re-pins position.z = previous.z = zLock and velocity.z = vzLock; a TELEPORT (a base position write) RE-ANCHORS zLock to the written z, and nothing re-anchors vzLock (the named v1 shape). Sprite colliders: collider="box" (the sprite default, also `auto`) derives from the sprite's SIZE as half extents [w/2, h/2, colliderHalfZ] with the pinned 1000 extrusion — so a box↔box contact's minimum-overlap axis is ALWAYS in the XY plane (the 2D semantics of an extruded rectangle) — centered on the QUAD CENTER (the anchor offset applied); collider="circle" (the alias of `sphere`) takes radius = half the SMALLER extent, min(w, h)/2, scaled by the largest world basis. The collider reads the RESOLVED `size`, so an unauthored size colliders as 1×1 (the texture aspect is a render-time refinement — the honest v1). Everything else — masses, restitution, friction, triggers, layers, sleep, characters, the fixed 60 Hz tick — is G2 verbatim. Case shape: `kind` selects the lane — quad (attrs [+ aspect] → the quad offset/half-extents) · uv (attrs → the frame's UV rect through the resolved+clamped frame index) · sheet (attrs → cols/rows/total/frame) · fps (attrs + elapsed samples → frame indices) · parse (markup → the typed IR + resolved props, worlds optional) · order (world z list → the 2D draw order) · physics-world (markup → the extracted body records) · physics-sim (specs + ticks → pinned states). `diagnostics` = expected count (absent = 0). All floats to 6 decimals, tolerance 1.5e-6; every number computed by an independent scratch implementation, never by a kernel under test. Runners: TS (per-PR) · Kotlin (:core, gradle) · Swift (record lane).
